ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Josephine Baker

code.originalText: Two-week review: echocardiogram, cardiology consultation the same day, the cause of the breathlessness and the antiplatelet plan

text.paragraph: Two-week review: echocardiogram, cardiology consultation and breathlessness. [S]

Ms. Baker returns two weeks after intake and is seen the same day by Dr. Mbeki-Fontaine of cardiology after her echocardiogram this morning. She is still breathless, but she describes it more exactly now: a sudden need to take a deep breath, often while sitting still or talking, as if she cannot get enough air, which began two or three days after she left the hospital. It does not build with effort the way it did on the day of the heart attack, and she has had no chest pressure, palpitations, ankle swelling, cough or waking at night breathless. She has taken every dose of aspirin, ticagrelor, atorvastatin, metoprolol and lisinopril, and has not needed nitroglycerin. Her home blood pressure averages 136/82. She has been to two cardiac rehabilitation sessions; on the treadmill she was not limited by breath. She is sleeping a little better. [S]

Adverse effect of antithrombotic drugs, initial encounter

list.item:
Breathlessness from ticagrelor (T45.525A). Air hunger at rest beginning days after ticagrelor was started, with normal oxygen saturation, clear lungs, no anemia (hemoglobin 12.2 g/dL), an ejection fraction of 52% with normal filling pressures and no angina, fits the breathlessness that ticagrelor causes in a minority of patients; it is not dangerous, but it is distressing and threatens adherence. Dr. Mbeki-Fontaine agrees. Deconditioning after the hospital stay adds to it. [S]
Stop ticagrelor; start clopidogrel with a 600 mg loading dose 24 hours after the last ticagrelor dose, then 75 mg daily.
Continue aspirin 81 mg.
Dual antiplatelet therapy for twelve months from the heart attack; never stop without speaking to cardiology.

Coronary artery disease after a non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (I25.10). No angina. Ejection fraction 52% with inferior hypokinesis from the infarct. Lipoprotein(a) 172 nmol/L, an inherited risk-enhancing level that strengthens the case for reaching the LDL goal. [S]
Continue atorvastatin 80 mg and metoprolol succinate 25 mg.
Lipid panel with the potassium check in one to two weeks, four to eight weeks after the statin start; ezetimibe if LDL is 70 mg/dL or higher.
Continue cardiac rehabilitation.

High blood pressure (I10). 136/82 in the clinic and at home, above the 130/80 target. [S]
Raise lisinopril to 10 mg daily.
Potassium and creatinine in one to two weeks.

Financial strain (Z59.86). Clopidogrel is a low-cost generic, which also helps. [S]
The social worker will see her at rehabilitation next week about debt advice.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes (2025); Acute Myocardial Infarction in Women: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association (2016); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, ischemic heart disease and acute myocardial infarction monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Metabolic panel in one to two weeks. Review in four weeks. Call for breathlessness that worsens, bleeding, or lightheadedness; call 911 for chest pain not relieved five minutes after one nitroglycerin. Next scheduled visit 2026-05-26: four-week review after the change to clopidogrel: breathlessness, blood pressure, potassium and kidney function, and cardiac rehabilitation. [S]
